title: Why an octopus has three hearts

beats.text: An octopus has three hearts. And one of them stops beating every time it swims.
Two of those hearts have a single job: pushing blood through the gills to pick up oxygen.
The third heart sends that fresh, oxygen-rich blood out to the arms, the organs and the brain.
And that blood is blue. Instead of iron, like ours, it carries oxygen with a copper protein called hemocyanin.
Hemocyanin works well in cold, low-oxygen water, exactly the kind of ocean many octopuses call home.
Now the catch. When an octopus jets through the water, the heart that feeds its body stops.
Swimming wears it out fast, which is one reason octopuses usually crawl instead.
Three hearts, and it would still rather walk.

sources: Wells et al., J. Exp. Biol. 1987
